short_description: An enveloped lentivirus (~100-125 nm) and the cat's own counterpart to HIV - closely related in architecture (envelope, matrix, conical capsid, two RNA copies, reverse transcriptase, integrase) but not infectious to people. Its Env spikes are notably SHORTER and sparser than HIV's, and its Gag proteins carry FIV-specific names (MA p15, CA p24, NC p13) rather than HIV's (p17/p24/p7) - related, not identical.
taxonomy: Family Retroviridae, genus Lentivirus (same genus as HIV; distinct from FeLV, a gammaretrovirus, and unrelated to it beyond both being feline retroviruses).

labels.la: glycoproteina superficiei, brevis et sparsa (SU gp95 / TM gp40)
labels.en: Env glycoprotein spike - short and sparse (SU gp95 / TM gp40)
labels.de: Hüllprotein-Spike - kurz und spärlich (SU gp95 / TM gp40)

do_not_draw: A non-enveloped / naked particle - FIV is always enveloped in a host-derived lipid bilayer.
An icosahedral or otherwise geometric-ball capsid - the mature core is a distinct CONE / truncated cone (wide at one end, narrower at the other), the single most checkable feature.
A double-stranded DNA genome inside the virion - the packaged genome is TWO COPIES of positive-sense single-stranded RNA (it only becomes DNA after reverse transcription inside the host cell).

Long, prominent, mushroom/club-stalked spikes copied straight from an HIV or coronavirus render - FIV's Env spikes are notably SHORTER and SPARSER than HIV's already-modest spikes; a dense fuzzy corona or tall stalked clubs are both wrong.
A bullet-shaped silhouette with a flat and a rounded end - that is rabies (a rhabdovirus, also in this set), not FIV; FIV is roughly spherical to ellipsoid.
A cat, a person, or any animal figure in the four science styles (sem/textbook/3d/watercolor) - those are molecule-scale renders of the virion alone.
Anything implying human infectivity - FIV cannot infect people; it is a cat-specific virus.
verification_note: Core shape confirmed as CONICAL (not spherical/icosahedral) per capsid crystallography and thin-section TEM of mature virions - checked explicitly on every accepted render (see render.md §5).

sources.claim: FIV virion ~100-125 nm diameter, spherical to ellipsoid; short envelope glycoprotein projections; conical shell (core) surrounded by an electron-dense nucleoid, separated from the plasma membrane by an electron-lucent space; mature particles (~125-150 nm) show condensed conical cores by thin-section TEM, vs. spherical cores lacking a dense centre in immature/budding particles.
sources.source: Properties and Functions of Feline Immunodeficiency Virus Gag Domains in Virion Assembly and Budding, PMC5977254

sources.claim: First atomic structure of full-length FIV capsid protein (CA, 1.67 Å) shows the same general two-domain alpha-helical fold as HIV-1 and EIAV CA despite low sequence identity (29%/39%); lentiviral CA proteins including FIV's assemble via hexamer/pentamer lattices into the cone-shaped (fullerene-geometry) mature core.
sources.source: Crystal Structure of the Full-Length Feline Immunodeficiency Virus Capsid Protein, PMC5707542

sources.claim: FIV Gag precursor Pr50Gag is cleaved by the viral protease into matrix (MA, p15), capsid (CA, p24), spacer p1, nucleocapsid (NC, p13) and spacer p2 - FIV-specific names/masses, distinct from HIV-1's MA p17 / CA p24 / NC p7, even though the same three structural roles exist in both viruses.
sources.source: Purification and Functional Characterization of a Biologically Active Full-Length FIV Pr50Gag, Viruses 2019, 11(8):689

sources.claim: FIV Env is processed into a surface subunit (SU, gp95) and a transmembrane subunit (TM, gp41/gp40 depending on source), non-covalently associated on the virion surface, structurally paralleling HIV-1 gp120/gp41 but with FIV-specific numbering; SU carries five variable regions (V1-V5).
sources.source: Mapping of the CXCR4 Binding Site within Variable Region 3 of the FIV Surface Glycoprotein, J Virol / PMC2546885; ScienceDirect topic pages on FIV Env processing

sources.claim: FIV Env spikes are described in current virology reviews as notably SHORT surface glycoprotein spikes embedded in the envelope (contrasted with HIV's spikes, which are themselves already sparse/short compared to many other enveloped viruses) - the teaching-relevant, checkable morphological difference between the two viruses for this atlas.
sources.source: Feline Immunodeficiency Virus (FIV): Virology, Diagnosis & Management - Bioguardlabs

sources.claim: FIV genome ~9400 nucleotides, three major genes gag/pol/env plus accessory genes, flanked by LTRs (shorter than HIV-1/SIV LTRs); Pol expressed via a Gag-Pol ribosomal frameshift and additionally encodes a dUTPase gene absent from primate lentiviruses (HIV, SIV) - a genuine FIV-vs-HIV genomic difference, not drawable but useful context for the scientific text.
sources.source: The Molecular Biology of Feline Immunodeficiency Virus (FIV), PMC3230847

sources.claim: Virion carries two copies of positive-sense single-stranded RNA plus reverse transcriptase, integrase and protease inside the conical core, matching the primate-lentivirus (HIV) packaging pattern.
sources.source: Feline Immunodeficiency Virus - overview, Advances in Small Animal Care / Veterian Key

sources.claim: Genus Lentivirus (ICTV): reference protein sizes MA ~17 kDa, CA ~24 kDa, NC 7-11 kDa, PR ~14 kDa, RT ~66 kDa, IN ~32 kDa, dUTPase ~14 kDa (present in all lentiviruses except the primate ones) - used as cross-check context; FIV's own Gag cleavage sizes (p15/p24/p13) are the ones used for FIV-specific labels.

reference_search_note: Extensively searched (Wikimedia Commons 'Category:Feline immunodeficiency virus' [14 files - all genome diagrams, an FIV.svg schematic, a rapid-test-kit photo, and a photo of a symptomatic cat; NO electron micrograph], CDC PHIL [no FIV entries exist - PHIL's lentivirus EM plates, e.g. #282, #10860, #18142/18143, are all HIV-1, not FIV], NIAID Flickr, PMC/PLOS open-access FIV papers [the Journal of Virology FIV-budding TEM paper (PMC2258934), which does contain FIV virion/budding EM figures, is Copyright American Society for Microbiology - NOT open-licensed; PLOS ONE / Veterinary World CC-BY FIV papers found in search were about diagnostics/molecular epidemiology, not EM plates]). CONCLUSION: no freely-licensed (PD/CC0/CC BY/CC BY-SA) photographic or micrograph reference of FIV virions could be located. Per pipeline policy this is reported plainly rather than substituting an HIV micrograph mislabelled as FIV. Step 2 (fetch_reference.py) is therefore skipped for this subject; the four science-style renders are the only imagery.
